note: A ONE-SURNAME genealogical databank, not a census index. Its Illinois page extracts Dalton, Dolton and Daulton entries — 'There are over 5000 surname entries in this file' — from census indexes, marriages, births, deaths, Chicago city directories, land sales and naturalizations. Its 1840 census block is 20 Illinois rows. Genealogy/index access path, not the census image, and a SURNAME databank rather than a city index — T-0497 read it whole and corrected the record, which had described it as a Chicago head-of-household index by ward. Retained as a later-Chicago identity candidate for one man; the index does not bridge the 1835 postal entry to the 1840 household, and the First Ward it names holds two Dalton households, not one. Rows in data/research/census_1840/records/dalton_index.json; adjudication in data/research/census_1840/dalton_index_crosswalk.json. NAMES ONLY are committed: the page's rights are check_required and a name index of a public-domain census is fact while the page is theirs.
what_it_supplies: 20 named Illinois heads of household in the 1840 federal census, surname Dalton, with a county and sometimes a precinct, township or Chicago ward
three of those rows in a Chicago ward: Edward Dalton (1st), Michael Dalton (2nd) and a surname-only 'Mr. Dalton' (1st)
an access path and a free, text, citable second-hand reading — the whole of it is at daltondatabank.net/Illinois.html

on its continuation page, Cook County federal land-sale rows for a George Dalton dated 25 and 27 June 1836, and one 1844 Chicago directory line (Michael Dalton, laborer, Water and Kinzie, res. Wolcott St.)
what_it_does_not_supply: any head of household not named Dalton, Dolton or Daulton — it is NOT a Chicago head-of-household index and cannot be a second reading of the 964 IPUMS households or of PR #670's 210 heads
household composition: no age bands, no counts, no line
the printed page and line of the census sheet, and no route back to the page image
any 1835 residence, and no bridge from an 1840 household back to 1835
ward boundaries: the ward is a number written into a place string, with no extent stated
access_notes: Fetched 2026-09-05, all HTTP 200: https://daltondatabank.net/ (41,224 bytes), https://daltondatabank.net/Illinois.html (165,061 bytes) and https://daltondatabank.net/Illinois_Page_2.html (204,480 bytes). There are no per-ward pages — the site's only Illinois pages are those two plus Newspapers/IllinoisNewspapers.htm, and the ward is a value inside a row — so `verified: true` means every page that exists was retrieved.
